reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
When Tracy left for school, the temperature was minus 3 degrees.

[Image: Thermometer showing minus 3 degrees]

At recess, the temperature was 5 degrees.

[Image: Thermometer showing 5 degrees]

How many degrees did the temperature rise?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two identical vertical thermometers are shown, one below the other:
1. The top thermometer has a scale marked with tick marks at intervals of 1 unit. Major tick marks are labeled on both sides at 10, 0, and -10. Intermediate longer tick marks appear at 5 and -5. The black liquid column rises from the bulb at the bottom to 3 units below 0 (-3 degrees).
2. The bottom thermometer has the same scale and markings (labeled at 10, 0, and -10). The black liquid column rises from the bulb to 5 units above 0 (5 degrees).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A number machine takes a number and operates on it.
When the Input Number is 5, the Output Number is 9, as shown below.

[Image: Number machine diagram]

When the Input Number is 7, which of these is the Output Number?
reference_items.figure_description:
A diagram of a number machine showing four geometric shapes connected horizontally by arrows:
1. A square containing the number "5", with the text "Input Number" centered directly above it.
2. An arrow pointing right labeled "× 2" leads to a circle containing the number "10".
3. An arrow pointing right labeled "+ 2" leads to another circle containing the number "12".
4. An arrow pointing right labeled "− 3" leads to an equilateral triangle containing the number "9", with the text "Output Number" centered directly above it.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Temperature for Week graph]

The graph above shows the daily high and low temperatures for a week.

On which day is the difference between the high and low temperatures the greatest?
reference_items.figure_description:
A plot titled "Temperature for Week". The vertical axis is labeled "Temperature" with grid lines marked at 20°, 25°, 30°, 35°, 40°, and 45°. The horizontal axis is labeled "Day" with vertical grid lines marked at Sun., Mon., Tues., Wed., Thu., Fri., and Sat.
A legend on the right shows a filled black circle labeled "High Temp." and an open circle labeled "Low Temp."
The points plotted for each day are:
- Sun.: High Temp. at 39°, Low Temp. at 25°
- Mon.: High Temp. at 42°, Low Temp. at 24°
- Tues.: High Temp. at ~34°, Low Temp. at ~28°
- Wed.: High Temp. at 30°, Low Temp. at 20°
- Thu.: High Temp. at 26°, Low Temp. at ~23°
- Fri.: High Temp. at ~36°, Low Temp. at 25°
- Sat.: High Temp. at 45°, Low Temp. at 30°
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Mary left Apton and rode at the same speed for 2 hours.

She reached this sign.

[Image: a girl on a bike facing right side stopping in front of a sign. The sign is written with “Brandon, 45 km” with a right arrow and “Apton, 30 km” with a left arrow.]

Mary continues to ride at the same speed to Brandon.

How many hours will it take her to ride from the sign to Brandon?
reference_items.figure_description: A silhouette of a girl on a bicycle facing right, stopped beside a rectangular road sign mounted on a post. The top section of the sign displays the text "Brandon, 45 km" followed by a right-pointing arrow (►). The bottom section displays a left-pointing arrow (◄) followed by the text "Apton, 30 km".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
